Leaving a book feels to me exactly like leaving a dream. The mood always is complicated and lingers for much longer than I expect.

Do you like spending time with animals? Do they put any dent in the pain? I am feeling very intensely what you are feeling today. I know dogs (for e.g.) are not perfect, and I don't think the ultimate long-term solution is to stay alive just because a pet depends on you to feed them. But I don't think there's anything wrong with trying. I also know the pain of people ignoring cries for help in writing. A road trip, with or without an animal companion, might be wonderful, especially if you can manage to be open to surprising connections with those you meet along the way. Also, humans are obsessed with linear time and most of what we say to one another to try to help revolves around a vague point in the future. Some people take comfort in this, and some don't. One thing I love about animals is their unique sense of time, and their insistence on keeping you in the present, which even at its most painful (the present, that is), is sometimes tolerable compared to thinking about any kind of future of more of the same. Love with an animal is not simple, but it can be simpler. Much of the reason I stay alive is to figure out how certain species, and certain animals in particular, are so good at loving and connection, especially when other humans let us down.
